# Citation gate — run 2026-08

Per standing rule: per-reference resolution at publisher record is mandatory before any GitHub Pages deployment. No reference appears in `index.html` that is not listed below as resolved.

## Resolved

### [1] Liu, Xia, Wang, Zhang (2023)
"Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation."
*Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems* 36 (NeurIPS 2023), 21558–21572. arXiv:2305.01210.
DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2305.01210 — **resolved at arXiv publisher record.**
v1 2 May 2023 · v3 30 Oct 2023.

Figures confirmed verbatim at abstract: 80x test augmentation; 26 models evaluated; pass@k reduced by up to 19.3–28.9%; mis-ranking finding; named pair WizardCoder-CodeLlama and Phind-CodeLlama outperforming ChatGPT on HumanEval+ where neither could on HumanEval.

**Field correction A.** Semantic Scholar's BibTeX renders the second author as "Chun Xia". Correct form is **Chunqiu Steven Xia**. Do not propagate the truncated form.

**Field correction B.** ACM DL renders the venue as *Proceedings of the 2024 International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems*, article 943. That is the 2024 publication date of the NeurIPS 2023 proceedings, not a separate conference. Cite as NeurIPS 2023 with the page range.

### [2] Chen, Tworek, Jun, et al. (2021)
"Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code." arXiv:2107.03374.
**Resolved.** Source of HumanEval. 164 hand-written problems; average 7.7 unit tests per problem.

**Open discrepancy.** Two secondary papers (2024–25) report approximately 9.6 test cases per problem rather than 7.7. Counting convention unresolved — possibly whether prompt-embedded example assertions are included. The primary's figure is used in the paper and the discrepancy is carried in the ledger rather than silently resolved.

### [3] Akhtar, Reuel, Soni, Ahuja, Ammanamanchi, Rawal, Zouhar, et al. (2026)
"When AI Benchmarks Plateau: A Systematic Study of Benchmark Saturation." arXiv:2602.16763, submitted 18 February 2026. Accepted at ICML 2026. 37 authors.
**Resolved at publisher record.** Dataset and code at the evaleval/benchmark-saturation repository.

Confirmed: 60 LLM benchmarks from major developers' technical reports; 14 properties; five hypotheses; nearly half saturated; saturation rates rise with age; hiding test data shows no protective effect; expert-curated benchmarks resist saturation better than crowdsourced.

**Note.** Confirmed at abstract and listing level. **Not read in full.** The paper's §7 claim that this dataset may hold part of the falsification test is therefore itself ungated.

## Not resolved, not cited

### §5 anchors
The historical claim that recording shifted the designation of musical authority from score to performance has **no anchor**.

Candidate sources were identified during drafting. They are **deliberately not named in this repository**. Naming plausible-looking titles in a verification document is precisely the citation-by-plausibility failure this gate exists to prevent, and a named-but-ungated reference has a way of migrating into a draft.

§5 is marked blocked in `index.html` and must not be deployed elsewhere in its present state.
